# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 4 (Bi-Vb Np4)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Aññaviññāpana* Sutta ("Asking for something else"), cataloged as Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 4 (Bi-Vb Np4), is a disciplinary rule from the Vinaya Piṭaka's Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga [SuttaCentral]. The rule governs the proper conduct of nuns regarding requisites, stipulating that a nun who asks for one particular item, but upon receiving it declares that she wants something else, commits an offense requiring forfeiture of the item and formal confession (*nissaggiya pācittiya*) [SuttaCentral]. An English translation of the rule and its accompanying case material has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].

Within the Pali canon, the rule has full parallels in the *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* (pli-tv-bi-pm-np4) and the *Bhikkhunī Parivāra* (Nissaggiya Pācittiya 4) [SuttaCentral]. Corresponding or resembling rules governing the improper requesting of requisites appear across multiple non-Theravāda Vinaya recensions, including the Dharmaguptaka (Lzh Dg Bi Vb Np 19), Mahīśāsaka (Lzh Mi Bi Vb Np 19), Sarvāstivāda (Lzh Sarv Bi Vb Np 25), and Mūlasarvāstivāda traditions extant in Chinese and Tibetan (such as xct-mu-bi-vb-np31) [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral also notes thematic links to the adjacent rule on changing an intended purchase (*Aññacetāpana*, Bi-Vb Np5) [SuttaCentral].

Text-reuse analysis conducted by DharmaNexus confirms extensive Pali-internal overlap with subsequent rules, displaying its closest structural affinity with Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 5 (segments §1.20–2.3.6 sharing high similarity with §1.21–2.28) and additional formulaic parallels across Nissaggiya Pācittiya 2, 6, 7, 10, and Khandhaka sections including the *Khuddakavatthukkhandhaka* (Kd 15) and *Bhikkhunikkhandhaka* (Kd 20) [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language matches, DharmaNexus automatically aligns passages of the text with the Tibetan translation of the *Bhikṣuṇīvinayavibhaṅga* (D0005) as well as the Tibetan *Pratimokṣasūtraṭīkāvinayasamuccaya* (D4106-2) and *Pratimokṣasūtravṛtti* (D4107) [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
